definition: The practice of deliberately probing an AI system for vulnerabilities, harmful outputs, or failure modes, typically before deployment.
details: Red teaming — whether performed by internal teams, external experts, or automated adversarial systems — is a key part of responsible AI development, surfacing risks like harmful content generation, bias, or susceptibility to jailbreaks.

explainer.lead: Deliberately probing an AI system for vulnerabilities, harmful outputs, or failure modes, typically before deployment. It matters because it surfaces risks before users encounter them.

tiers.eli5: It's like hiring someone to try every trick to break into your house before you move in, so you can fix the weak spots first.
tiers.practitioner: Run by internal teams, external experts, or automated adversarial systems as part of responsible AI development; the pitfall is stopping at obvious attacks and missing subtler failures.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the practice of deliberately probing an AI system for vulnerabilities, harmful outputs, or failure modes, typically before deployment, surfacing risks like harmful content generation, bias, or susceptibility to jailbreaks.

explainer.example: An external expert team tries jailbreak prompts against a chatbot before launch and reports the ones that produce harmful content.
